## Source: amazon-inspector (ba05c76200656d6746f6f200e1e45f8027d4c87bb6b2312b9690aad262ddf39c)
tailwindcss-form-ui@0.5.8 impersonates @tailwindcss/forms: package.json sets author to '@tailwindcss' and repository to https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss-forms while publishing under an unrelated name, and the README and plugin source are verbatim copies of the real @tailwindcss/forms with a malicious preamble added. The declared main entry src/index.js prepends ~15 KB of obfuscated code to the copied plugin. A custom deterministic string-shuffle primitive (functions named spin/peel/splitLane with hardcoded seed arrays) reconstructs the identifiers 'constructor', 'require', 'module', and 'global' at runtime, then invokes the Function constructor on a decoded code blob and immediately calls the resulting function with require bound as a local parameter: Forge('z', peel('<decoded body>'))(require). This executes attacker-controlled code with full Node module access the moment any consumer require()s the package. A Tailwind CSS plugin has no legitimate need to construct and run dynamically-decoded code at import time or to pass require into it; the obfuscation primitive exists only to hide the stager from static review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
